title: Cape Romain partnership for coastal protection
citation: Eaton, M.J., Johnson, F.A., Mikels-Carrasco, Jessica, Case, D.J., Martin, Julien, Stith, Bradley, Yurek, Simeon, Udell, Bradley, Villegas, Laura, Taylor, Laura, Haider, Zulquarnain, Charkhgard, Hadi, and Kwon, Changhyun, 2021, Cape Romain partnership for coastal protection: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report OF-2021-1021, map scale 1:224,700.
notes:
Packet is front matter, introduction and the start of the sea-level-rise chapter of a coastal conservation planning report; no map units, borings, wells, structures or aquifer data. Vertical datum note (NAVD 88, p. 13) is a general report statement, not tied to any geologic value. Only references relevant to South Carolina coastal geology and hydrology are recorded; governance, social-science and general climate references skipped. SUBSURFACE: none.
Packet covers sea-level-rise projections, storm surge and barrier-island erosion at Cape Romain. Geomorphic statements (barrier islands transgressing shoreward, Cape Romain a cuspate foreland, Santee River delta transformed from progradational to regressive after damming, shoreline retreat about 6 m per year 1941-1973, island acreage changes 1875-2011, Hugo erosion 20-25 m and dune erosion 90-180 m, muddy marsh deposits outcropping across the receding beach) have no field in the schema and are not recorded. The tectonic downwarp is reported second-hand (Hayes and Sexton, 1989) and recorded as a structure with no location beyond the study area. Storm-tide elevations (Hugo, p. 33, 37) are hydrologic, not geologic surfaces, and are not recorded. Stakeholder pages 55-61 hold no geology. Only references relevant to South Carolina coastal geology are recorded. SUBSURFACE: none.
Packet covers stakeholder engagement, scenario planning and the SWOT analysis (pages 62-85). No geologic units, observations, structures, aquifer data or South Carolina geology references; the mention of saltwater intrusion into freshwater aquifers (p. 74) is part of a hypothetical future scenario, not a finding, and is not recorded. SUBSURFACE: none.
Packet covers the SWOT tables and the reserve-design and portfolio optimization of habitat parcels (pages 86-115), based on modeled habitat (SLAMM) areas. No geologic units, observations, structures, aquifer data or South Carolina geology references. SUBSURFACE: none.
